  If this is your first time, check out https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests-prs
  for our PR guidelines.
-->

## Problem

1. The default statusline displays diagnotics even when diagnostics are disabled
2. `vim.diagnostic.count()` counts diagnostics across all buffers by default, while `vim.diagnostic.status()` acts on the current buffer by default. This result in unnecessary `vim.diagnostic.status()` calls when diagnostics exist in other buffers but not in the current buffer

## Solution

1. Add `vim.diagnostic.is_enabled()` check to the diagnostics condition
2. Use `vim.g.actual_curbuf` throughout the diagnostics condition to check against the real current buffer

comment_data.body:
actually, since `vim.diagnostic.status` , and even `vim.diagnostic.is_enabled / count` , are intended to be used in the statusline, maybe they can just handle `0` like this:

```lua
buf = buf ~= 0 and buf or tonumber(vim.g.actual_curbuf) or ...
```

that avoids this cruft in the stl expr, and also avoids creating a closure every time it's evaluated (doesn't matter but still feels yucky)

and tbh, that treatment of `buf=0` should be the standard across the codebase:

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/350fa5ad7ccc014bcdd0eea2bd76ba09a265452e/runtime/lua/vim/_core/shared.lua#L1664

maybe it even makes sense for `vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()` to do it...

comment_regular_data.body:
The change with Justin's suggestion and reasoning look good .

This is outside of the scope of this PR but it does get progressively more complex as we pile things into the this one part of statusline. Perhaps we can consider having toggle-able sections of statusline.

the `vim._resolve_bufnr` change is worth exploring but i think it's too risky and should be a separate effort. it may introduce weird problems if lsp/treesitter/whatever does work in "temporary buffers" during statusline eval.

for now, i think a good approach is to add a `statusline:bool` param to `status()` :

```diff
diff --git i/runtime/lua/vim/diagnostic.lua w/runtime/lua/vim/diagnostic.lua
index cbd7e8f5d15d..efbb224fd072 100644
--- i/runtime/lua/vim/diagnostic.lua
+++ w/runtime/lua/vim/diagnostic.lua
@@ -1112,13 +1112,24 @@ local default_status_signs = {
 ---
 --- To customise appearance, see |vim.diagnostic.Opts.Status|.
 ---
----@param buf? integer Buffer number to get diagnostics from.
----                      Defaults to 0 for the current buffer
+--- Recommended 'statusline' usage:
+--- ```vim
+---   %{% luaeval("(package.loaded['vim.diagnostic'] and vim.diagnostic.status(0, true)) or ''") %}
+--- ```
 ---
----@return string
-function M.status(buf)
+---@param buf? integer Buffer number to get diagnostics from. Defaults to 0 (current buffer).
+---@param statusline? boolean For use in 'statusline'. Prefers `g:actual_curbuf` if buf=0/nil.
+---       Returns nil if diagnostics are disabled/empty.
+---@return string?
+function M.status(buf, statusline)
   vim.validate('buf', buf, 'number', true)
-  buf = buf or 0
+  vim.validate('statusline', statusline, 'boolean', true)
+
+  buf = statusline and (buf == nil or buf == 0) and tonumber(vim.g.actual_curbuf) or buf or 0
+  if statusline and not M.is_enabled({ bufnr = buf }) then
+    return nil
+  end
+
   local config = assert(vim.diagnostic.config()).status or {} --- @type vim.diagnostic.Opts.Status
   vim.validate('config.format', config.format, 'function', true)
 
@@ -1138,11 +1149,14 @@ function M.status(buf)
       :join(' ')
   end
 
-  if result_str:len() > 0 then
-    result_str = result_str .. '%##'
+  if result_str:len() == 0 then
+    if statusline then
+      return nil
+    end
+    return ''
   end
 
-  return result_str
+  return result_str .. '%##'
 end
 
 nvim_on('DiagnosticChanged', api.nvim_create_augroup('nvim.diagnostic.status'), {
diff --git i/src/nvim/options.lua w/src/nvim/options.lua
index c23e6e7e0fc1..f500c38cf4e4 100644
--- i/src/nvim/options.lua
+++ w/src/nvim/options.lua
@@ -9120,7 +9120,7 @@ local options = {
           '%(%-10S %)',
           "%{ &busy > 0 ? '◐\226\128\175' : '' }", -- use non-breaking space to avoid fillchar

-          "%{% luaeval('(package.loaded[''vim.diagnostic''] and next(vim.diagnostic.count(0)) and vim.diagnostic.status() .. '' '') or '''' ') %}",
+          "%(%{% luaeval('(package.loaded[''vim.diagnostic''] and vim.diagnostic.status(0, true)) or '''' ') %} %)",
           '%(%k %)',
           "%{% &ruler ? &rulerformat : '' %}",
         }),
diff --git i/test/functional/ui/statusline_spec.lua w/test/functional/ui/statusline_spec.lua
index a1b3a5322892..3338eebdb79e 100644
--- i/test/functional/ui/statusline_spec.lua
+++ w/test/functional/ui/statusline_spec.lua
@@ -1158,7 +1158,7 @@ describe('default statusline', function()

       "%(%{ luaeval('(package.loaded[''vim.ui''] and vim.api.nvim_get_current_win() == tonumber(vim.g.actual_curwin or -1) and vim.ui.progress_status()) or '''' ')} %)",
-      "%{% luaeval('(package.loaded[''vim.diagnostic''] and next(vim.diagnostic.count(0)) and vim.diagnostic.status() .. '' '') or '''' ') %}",
+      "%(%{% luaeval('(package.loaded[''vim.diagnostic''] and vim.diagnostic.status(0, true)) or '''' ') %} %)",
       '%(%k %)',
       "%{% &ruler ? &rulerformat : '' %}",
     })
```

Thanks for the detailed proposal @justinmk!

Unfortunately, from my testing, `%(...%)` does not seem to work with `%{%...%}`, which makes adding the ending space not possible without a more quirky expression. Should I just go back to the original closure solution or is this worth a deeper dive into why the combination doesn't work?
that's just a typo... i didn't actually test the statusline expr
Sorry for being a little slow here but where is the typo actually?

Removing `%(...%)` seems to work but the ending space persists even when there are no diagnostics:
```diff
- "%(%{% luaeval('(package.loaded[''vim.diagnostic''] and vim.diagnostic.status(0, true)) or '''' ') %} %)",
+ "%{% luaeval('(package.loaded[''vim.diagnostic''] and vim.diagnostic.status(0, true)) or '''' ') %} ",
```

my suggestion was a sketch... not a full solution. otherwise i would have created a PR

surely the space is just a small logic bug

> `%(...%)` does not seem to work with `%{%...%}`

It currently works in a way that makes some sense, but not in a way that is helpful in this situation. First, the result of the expression in `%{%...%}` is inserted, then the item group works in the usual way with the result. The usual auto-hiding only works well with items that can show information, and in this case there are no such items in the result, only items that change highlighting. Note that `%{...}` would have worked in this case, but it doesn't support highlighting.

Unfortunately, for now, I think it's easiest to add the space inside `status()`:
```lua
  if statusline then
    return result_str:len() > 0 and result_str .. '%## ' or nil
  end
  return result_str:len() > 0 and result_str .. '%##' or ''
```
Maybe the value of the statusline parameter can decide whether the space is added on the left or on the right?

A lua helper could be useful that conditionally concatenates two values if both are non-empty strings, and otherwise returns an empty string:
```
stl_concat(package.loaded['vim.diagnostic'] and vim.diagnostic.status(0), ' ')
```
At some point, the statusline should probably have proper support for lua, so that `luaeval` isn't needed and some statusline-specific functions like that helper or `term_exitcode` can just be used without being imported. Something like this:
```
%{`lua` term_exitcode() }
```

BTW: personally, I would prefer not to use `g:actual_curbuf`, I think every window should have the window-local diagnostics in its own status line. With `g:actual_curbuf`, every window's status line has the same diagnostics of the window currently focused by the user.

Thanks @epithet for your constructive comments.

> Unfortunately, for now, I think it's easiest to add the space inside `status()`:
> ```lua
>   if statusline then
>     return result_str:len() > 0 and result_str .. '%## ' or nil
>   end
>   return result_str:len() > 0 and result_str .. '%##' or ''
> ```

This was my thought also, which makes the functionality not flexible.

> Maybe the value of the statusline parameter can decide whether the space is added on the left or on the right?
>
> A lua helper could be useful that conditionally concatenates two values if both are non-empty strings, and otherwise returns an empty string:
> ```
> stl_concat(package.loaded['vim.diagnostic'] and vim.diagnostic.status(0), ' ')
> ```

This could resolve the above concern but may need careful design, which I think is out of scope for this particular issue.

> BTW: personally, I would prefer not to use g:actual_curbuf, I think every window should have the window-local diagnostics in its own status line. With g:actual_curbuf, every window's status line has the same diagnostics of the window currently focused by the user.

Thanks for pointing this out, I have `laststatus=3` in my config so the quirk is simply glossed over during testing.

If @justinmk is ok with it then we could go with the original change:
```diff
- %{% luaeval('(package.loaded[''vim.diagnostic''] and next(vim.diagnostic.count(0)) and vim.diagnostic.status() .. '' '') or '''' ') %}
+ %{% luaeval('(package.loaded[''vim.diagnostic''] and vim.diagnostic.is_enabled({bufnr = 0}) and next(vim.diagnostic.count(0)) and vim.diagnostic.status() .. '' '') or '''' ') %}
```

> This could resolve the above concern but may need careful design, which I think is out of scope for this particular issue.

Probably, particularly this close to a release. Consider my comment just a brainstorm.

Hi @justinmk, I modified the solution to directly filter for enabled diagnostics by passing `{ enabled = true }` to `vim.diagnostic.count()`. The change to the statusline expression is less verbose than the original solution.
